findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are hard-coded in plaintext in the Lambda function's environment variables. Anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration, console read access, or state file access can read these long-lived credentials and use them directly.

The Lambda function defines environment variables holding secrets but sets no kms_key_arn, so the values are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key and are readable by any principal with basic Lambda read permissions rather than being gated behind a customer-managed KMS key policy.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which has reached end of life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving the execution environment exposed to unpatched vulnerabilities.

The function has no vpc_config, so it runs outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or network segmentation controls, easing exfiltration of the embedded credentials if the function is compromised.
